title: Charting circumstellar chemistry of carbon-rich asymptotic giant branch stars. I. ALMA 3 mm spectral surveys
question: Obtain a more generalised understanding of the chemistry in C-rich AGB circumstellar envelopes by studying three carbon stars (IRAS 15194-5115, IRAS 15082-4808, IRAS 07454-7112) and observationally test the archetypal status of IRC +10 216.

recipe.goal: Continuum imaging and subtraction, spectral extraction, and line identification
recipe.method: Image continuum from line-free channels across 85-116 GHz using multi-frequency synthesis, subtract continuum from visibilities, extract spectra from 12.5'' radius circular apertures centred on continuum peaks (and molecule-specific apertures of radius R_p + 2.5*HWHM), and identify lines using spectroscopic catalogues.
key_parameters: Survey aperture radius = 12.5''; molecule-specific aperture radius = R_p + 2.5 * HWHM; detection threshold = 3 sigma
assumptions: All observed SiS line emissions are assumed to be primarily thermal in nature.

recipe.goal: Assess line variability between observation epochs
recipe.method: Compare spectra produced from a subset of visibilities sharing the same uv-coverage between the 2015 and 2016 datasets to isolate time-dependent amplitude variations.
assumptions: Spatial expansion of the circumstellar gas over <=1 yr (~6 mas) is negligible compared to the beam size.

recipe.goal: Stack systemic-velocity emission maps to study CSE substructure
recipe.method: Regrid line cubes to a common 3.3 km/s spectral resolution and velocity grid, and stack systemic-velocity channels across all detected Band 3 transitions per molecule using rms-weighted mean.
key_parameters: Spectral resolution = 3.3 km/s; no channel averaging; radial cuts at PA = 0 deg and PA = 90 deg

recipe.goal: Determine radial extents (R_i, R_e) of molecular emitting regions via AARPs
recipe.method: Convolve non-blended line cubes to a common circular beam, average channels within ±20% of v_exp around v_sys, compute azimuthally-averaged radial profiles in concentric rings of width equal to the common beam, average line profiles weighted by inverse squared uncertainty, and fit Gaussians to derive beam-deconvolved inner and outer radii.
key_parameters: Velocity range = v_sys ± 0.2 * v_exp; ring width = common restoring beam; centrally-peaked: R_i = 0, R_e = HWHM; shell: R_i, R_e = half-maxima points on either side of peak R_p
assumptions: Rarer isotopologues of HCN, CS, SiO, and HC3N are co-spatial with their main counterparts since photodissociation occurs via broadband continuum.

recipe.goal: Estimate rotational temperatures and column densities using population diagrams
recipe.method: For species with >=3 rotational transitions (combining ALMA and APEX lines), perform linear fit of ln(N_u/g_u) vs E_u/k_B with C_tau = 1, compute line optical depths tau_nu, apply optical depth correction factor C_tau, and re-fit to obtain optical-depth-corrected T_rot and N_tot.
key_parameters: Minimum 3 transitions required; optical depth correction factor C_tau = tau / (1 - exp(-tau))
assumptions: LTE Boltzmann level populations described by a single rotational temperature T_rot; linear rigid rotor partition functions for all species except asymmetric tops SiC2 and c-C3H2 (interpolated from CDMS); no hyperfine structure for partition functions/degeneracies when summing hyperfine fluxes.

recipe.goal: Calculate molecular fractional abundances and isotopic ratios
recipe.method: Convert N_tot from population diagrams to fractional abundance f_X = n(X)/n(H2) using Eq. E.6 and AARP radii; for species without population diagrams, compute f_X analytically from the highest-SNR single line using Eq. E.7; derive isotopic ratios from abundance ratios (when population diagrams exist) or line intensity ratios.
key_parameters: Assumed T_ex = 40 K (centrally-peaked) and 20 K (shell) for single-line estimates; distances, MLRs, and v_exp from Table 1
assumptions: Isotropic, constant mass-loss rate CSE expanding at terminal velocity with r^-2 density distribution; constant fractional abundance between R_i and R_e and zero outside; optically thin lines for single-line estimates; identical excitation conditions for isotopologue transitions.

evidence.quote: We detect, above the 3σ noise level, a total of 314 spectral emission features across the three stars, out of which 311 could be identified and assigned to 132 known rotational transitions of 49 molecular species

score_reason: The reprocessed ALMA image cubes, extracted spectra, and integrated intensity tables (including APEX lines) are publicly released at CDS, and the mathematical recipes for AARPs, population diagrams (Eqs. E.2-E.5), and abundance conversions (Eqs. E.6-E.7) are explicitly written out with all source parameters in Table 1. Minor deductions for unstated tclean imaging parameters (cell size, multiscale scales) and exact quasar flux calibration values.
rediscovery_reason: Both raw ALMA data and the authors' reprocessed cubes/spectra are public (ALMA Archive and CDS), and the downstream analysis (Gaussian fits to AARPs for 14 species, optical-depth-corrected population diagrams, and analytical abundance/isotopic ratio calculations) is self-contained and yields extensive numeric tables (Tables 4-8, B.1).
